chunks: Muhammad ibn Musa ibn al-Mutawakkil (may God have mercy on him) narrated to us. He said: Ali ibn Ibrahim ibn Hashim narrated to us from Muhammad ibn Isa ibn Ubayd, from Yunus ibn Abd al-Rahman, from Dawud ibn Farqad, from Ibn Shubruma.

He said: I never mentioned a hadith that I heard from Ja'far ibn Muhammad (peace be upon him) except that my heart would nearly break for him. I heard him say: My father narrated to me from my grandfather, from the Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family).
Ibn Shubruma said: And I swear by God, he would not lie upon his father, and his father would not lie upon his grandfather, and his grandfather would not lie upon the Messenger of God.

He said: Whoever acts by analogical reasoning (qiyas) is destroyed and has destroyed others. And whoever issues religious rulings to the people while he does not know the abrogating from the abrogated, nor the decisive from the allegorical, is destroyed and has destroyed others.

key_terms.النَّاسِخَ: Nasikh — the abrogating verse or ruling that supersedes an earlier one
key_terms.الْمَقَايِيسِ: Qiyas — analogical reasoning in Islamic law, condemned here as a method of independent juristic speculation divorced from prophetic guidance
key_terms.الْمَنْسُوخِ: Mansukh — the abrogated verse or ruling that has been superseded
key_terms.الْمُتَشَابِهِ: Mutashabih — allegorical, ambiguous verses requiring interpretation
key_terms.الْمُحْكَمَ: Muhkam — clear, decisive verses whose meaning is unambiguous

ai.seo_question: What did the Prophet say about acting on qiyas and issuing fatwas without knowledge of abrogation?
ai.summary: This hadith, narrated by Ibn Shubruma — likely a Kufan jurist who encountered Imam al-Sadiq — relays a prophetic teaching transmitted through the Imam's father and grandfather. It contains two related prohibitions: acting on qiyas (analogical reasoning) without divine guidance, and issuing fatwas without mastering the Quranic sciences of abrogation (naskh) and the distinction between muhkam (decisive) and mutashabih (allegorical) verses. The historical context is the early Islamic period when jurisprudential schools were forming, and the Imam's emphasis on authenticated chain-transmission over speculative reasoning reflects a core Shia hermeneutical position.

en.bilal-muhammad: Muhammad b. Musa b. al-Mutawakkil (rh) narrated to us. He said: `Ali b. Ibrahim b. Hashim narrated to us from Muhammad b. `Isa b. `Ubayd from Yunus b. `Abd al-Rahman from Dawud b. Farqad from Ibn Shabrama.

He said: I never mentioned a hadith that I heard from Ja`far b. Muhammad (as) except that my heart would break for him. I heard him say: My father narrated to me from my grandfather from the Messenger of Allah (s).
Ibn Shabrama said: By Allah, he would not lie upon his father, and his father would not lie upon his grandfather, and his grandfather would not lie upon the Messenger of Allah.

He [(s)] said: Whoever acts by analogies (qiyas) is destroyed and has destroyed others. Whoever gave rulings to the people without knowing the abrogating from the abrogated nor the decisive from the allegorical is destroyed and has destroyed others.
